sentences.text: Solicitor Priya Mehta attended the meeting with client Kerry Dobson to prepare for a hearing on 15 December and review the local authority's letter.
Client Kerry Dobson stated that contact with Tyler is currently good, occurring Tuesdays and Thursdays at the family centre on Mill Lane.
Client Kerry Dobson reported that Tyler keeps asking when he can come home.
Client Kerry Dobson reported that Tyler lost his front tooth.
Client Kerry Dobson reported that Tyler likes the foster carers and that they have a dog.
Client Kerry Dobson confirmed Tyler is still at Ashgrove Primary, driven in by the carers.
Client Kerry Dobson reported that Tyler's teacher says he is doing better with his reading.
Client Kerry Dobson disclosed that she used crack last weekend, stating it was just once.
Client Kerry Dobson initially denied using crack after disclosing it, stating 'No, forget I said that. It was nothing. I'm fine, honestly, I'm clean.'
Client Kerry Dobson confirmed she used crack on Saturday night at her cousin's flat.
Client Kerry Dobson disclosed that she has been using heroin again since 3 November.
Client Kerry Dobson stated she uses heroin every day, smoking it rather than injecting.
Client Kerry Dobson reported the cost of heroin is about £40 a day.
Client Kerry Dobson disclosed she is paying for heroin using her Universal Credit and borrowing money from her nan, who believes it is for gas.
Client Kerry Dobson stated she stopped picking up her script about three weeks ago.
Client Kerry Dobson confirmed she still lives at the flat on Corporation Street.
Client Kerry Dobson stated rent is paid directly but she is behind on council tax.
Client Kerry Dobson asked if contact would stop if the hair-strand test came back positive.
Client Kerry Dobson stated she has a naloxone kit somewhere but it is probably out of date.
Client Kerry Dobson stated her primary objective is for Tyler to come home.
Solicitor Priya Mehta advised that a hair test usually covers about three months, meaning the disclosed drug use is likely to show up.
Solicitor Priya Mehta advised that it is better for the client to tell the social worker before the test result if she is already back in treatment, as this looks different to the.
Solicitor Priya Mehta stated that courts do not usually stop contact over a relapse alone if the client is turning up sober and engaging, but noted that hiding it is what worries.
Solicitor Priya Mehta stated she cannot file a statement saying the client is clean.
Solicitor Priya Mehta disclosed that the risk of overdose is highest when going back to heroin after a break.
Solicitor Priya Mehta advised the client to get a new naloxone kit from the Recovery Hub, which will provide one the same day.
Solicitor Priya Mehta instructed the client to ring the Harbridge Recovery Hub and ask to restart their script by Friday 27 November.
Client Kerry Dobson stated she will go to the Recovery Hub tomorrow.
Solicitor Priya Mehta instructed the client to think about telling the social worker, Ms Carter, and to let the solicitor know by Monday whether she wants the solicitor to write to
Solicitor Priya Mehta stated she will send a letter confirming her advice today and will chase the local authority for the date of the test.
Solicitor Priya Mehta instructed the client to keep going to contact on Tuesday and Thursday, every time.
Solicitor Priya Mehta instructed the client to bring in the latest council tax bill to discuss a payment plan.
Solicitor Priya Mehta confirmed the next appointment is 8 December at 10:00.
